Connor / Ben — looping in my notes so we present a defensible exhibit to Acme: 

1) Modeling assumptions
- Commit smoothing should default to monthly smoothing using actual monthly consumption with a 12-month true-up. We'll show both a straight smoothing (evenly distributed) and actuals-based monthly smoothing.
- Distributor commission tiers (example): 0–$250k = 10%, $250k–$750k = 7.5%, >$750k = 5%. We'll parameterize these so legal/revops can change them.

2) Invoice routing options (pros/cons)
- Single invoice to Acme with downstream allocation: simpler for Acme AP, Redwood issues one invoice and then pays Brightline via our partner settlement flow. Pro: single payment, simpler reconciliation for Acme. Con: requires reseller agreement and mapping fields in our accounting system.
- Split invoice (Acme pays Redwood and Brightline separately): Brightline appears on the invoice and collects their share directly. Pro: clean separation of obligations. Con: more complex procurement for Acme.

3) Evidence pickup for procurement packet
- We'll prepare a 1-page settlement note, the waterfall spreadsheet, and a reseller agreement draft redline. Ask Acme for their ERP fields and preferred remit-to.

Ben — any constraints on minimum invoice amount / quarter-month cutoffs? If we need to move to quarterly invoices for Brightline to make economics work, call it out in the exhibit.

Irene
Partner Operations, Redwood Inference
